steps.description:
You will be guided in using AI to support your learning journey.

Read the topic on "Compatibility with AI".

Link to AI notes


Snake is a classic game that many has played. The game is also popularly used as a coding exercise.

Ask the AI module to create a snake game using Python. It should be able to control the snake with WASD.

Run it on any online IDE such as Replit.com, Trinket.io, etc. Does it work?


What you can learn from this exercise:

1. AI generated code may be correct. However, if you run it on an a platform that doesn't support certain Python libraries, it may not execute properly.

2. Are you able to understand the generated code enough such that you can tweak it manually? To make it work or be more specific in your prompt.






.

Use an AI model to implement the rotate() function below to turn the matrix as shown in the test output.

All added code must be within the rotate function and no where else including the main.


import random

def display(map):
    for i in range(len(map)):
        print(*map[i])
    print()

def rotate(map):
    pass

row = random.randint(2, 5)
col = random.randint(2, 5)
matrix = [[_ for _ in range(col)] for __ in range(row)]

print(row, "by", col, "matrix:")
display(matrix)
rotate(matrix)


Sample output when the program is run:

   

What you can learn from this exercise:

1. Very often, you need to add functions to your existing code. What happen if your current code is too large to be pasted into the AI model? Can you still prompt it accurately to get what you want?

2. AI may not interpret images directly. Sometimes you may have to translate your request.







.
